subject: vervet monkey
title: Vervet Monkeys Use 3 Different Alarm Calls for 3 Different Killers

scenes.text: One scream sends these monkeys up a tree. Another makes them stare at the ground.
Vervet monkeys in Kenya face three big killers: leopards, eagles and pythons.
Each killer gets its own alarm call. Leopard call: everyone runs up into the trees.
Eagle call: they look up at the sky and duck into bushes. Snake call: they look down.
In 1980, scientists hid a speaker and played the calls with no predator around. The monkeys did exactly the same.
So that scream doesn't just mean danger. It names the killer.

description:
One alarm call sends vervet monkeys up a tree; another makes them stare at the ground.
In Amboseli National Park, Kenya, vervets give different alarm calls to leopards, martial eagles and pythons. When Robert Seyfarth, Dorothy Cheney and Peter Marler played recorded alarms from hidden speakers with no predator present (Science, 1980), the monkeys ran into trees for leopard alarms, looked up for eagle alarms and looked down for snake alarms. Infants call at the wrong animals at first and get more precise with age.
Which animal do you think has the smartest warning system?
first_comment: Baby vervets get it wrong at first and sound the eagle alarm at harmless birds. Adults look around before trusting a youngster's call. Smart?
